cheatSheet.oneLineDefinition: Cloud warehouses eliminate redundant work through three levers: result cache (return stored output for identical re-runs), materialized views (precompute expensive aggregations), and partition/micro-partition pruning (skip irrelevant data at scan time).
keyConcepts: Result cache: exact-match query + unchanged data + deterministic functions = instant reuse, zero compute cost.
Materialized view: precomputed SELECT stored as a table; auto-refreshed; transparently rewrites incoming queries on all three platforms.
Partition pruning (BigQuery): PARTITION BY + WHERE filter on partition column = skip partitions; no filter = full scan.
Micro-partition pruning (Snowflake): automatic per-column min/max metadata on ~16 MB blocks; any column filter can prune.
Zone maps (Redshift): same concept as micro-partitions but require SORTKEY + VACUUM SORT to be effective.
Automatic Clustering (Snowflake): reorganizes micro-partitions by clustering key columns to improve pruning effectiveness.

Three levers compared: caching = zero recomputation (exact repeats only); MV = precomputed work (flexible queries, refresh cost); pruning = less data read per query (no precomputation, always effective).
commands:
-- Snowflake: disable result cache for testing
ALTER SESSION SET USE_CACHED_RESULT = FALSE;

-- Snowflake: check cache hit and pruning in query history
SELECT bytes_scanned, partitions_scanned, partitions_total FROM TABLE(INFORMATION_SCHEMA.QUERY_HISTORY_BY_SESSION());

-- BigQuery: dry run to preview bytes scanned (free)
bq query --dry_run --use_legacy_sql=false '<your_sql>'

-- BigQuery: check cache hit in JOBS_BY_PROJECT
SELECT cache_hit, total_bytes_billed FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS_BY_PROJECT ORDER BY creation_time DESC LIMIT 10;

-- Redshift: check MV freshness
SELECT mv_name, state FROM STL_MV_STATE;

-- Redshift: manual MV refresh
REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW schema.mv_name;

-- BigQuery: create MV with auto-refresh
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW project.dataset.mv_name OPTIONS (enable_refresh=true, refresh_interval_minutes=60) AS SELECT ...;
interviewPoints: Result cache: identical query text + no DML on referenced tables + no non-deterministic functions = cache hit (zero cost).
MV auto-rewrite: user queries base table, engine silently rewrites to hit MV — no SQL changes needed (Snowflake Enterprise, BigQuery, Redshift).
BigQuery partition pruning requires explicit PARTITION BY at table creation AND a matching WHERE clause on the partition column — missing either means full table scan.
Snowflake micro-partition pruning is automatic for all columns; Automatic Clustering improves it for columns with poor natural ordering.
Three levers: cache (free, exact repeat), MV (precomputed, maintenance cost, flexible queries), pruning (per-query I/O reduction, no precomputation).
quickNotes: Non-deterministic functions (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, RANDOM()) permanently disable result cache for that query on all three platforms.
Snowflake result cache persists through warehouse suspension (stored in Cloud Services layer); warehouse block cache does not survive suspension.
BigQuery: PARTITION BY ingestion time (_PARTITIONTIME) vs column — column partitioning is usually better (aligned with query filters).
Redshift: VACUUM SORT is the prerequisite for effective zone map pruning — without it, zone maps degrade over time for append-heavy tables.
MV maintenance cost rule of thumb: MV saves money when the cost of N query scans of the base table > cost of M MV refreshes + N MV scans (where N >> M).

keyTakeaways: Result caches, materialized views, and partition/micro-partition pruning are three distinct, complementary optimization levers: result caching avoids recomputation for exact query repeats; materialized views precompute expensive aggregations at refresh time so queries scan a tiny precomputed result; pruning reduces the raw data read per query execution.

Result cache invalidation is always triggered by data modification — a background pipeline modifying a table every 5 minutes will produce a 0% cache hit rate regardless of how 'identical' the queries appear. Non-deterministic functions also permanently disable caching.

Materialized views on all three platforms (Snowflake Enterprise, BigQuery, Redshift) support automatic query rewriting, meaning existing queries benefit from a new MV without any SQL changes — making MVs safe to introduce incrementally without application coordination.

Snowflake provides automatic fine-grained micro-partition pruning on every column without user-defined partition schemes; BigQuery requires explicit PARTITION BY and a matching WHERE clause to prune; Redshift requires COMPOUND SORTKEY and regular VACUUM SORT to maintain effective zone map pruning.

The highest ROI optimization strategy for established analytical workloads is: (1) audit result cache hit rates and fix non-deterministic queries, (2) build MVs for the top 5 most expensive repeated aggregation patterns, (3) confirm partition/clustering design eliminates 90%+ of data scans for filter-heavy queries — together, these three steps typically reduce warehouse compute cost by 70-90%.
